quizzes.title: Reformed Multilateralism: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The 81st United Nations General Assembly opened on 8 September 2026 in New York, under the theme "Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All." On its sidelines, India's External Affairs Minister co-chaired the inaugural Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa. The P4M framework is built on the middle-power solidarity idea that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney set out at Davos. It was conceived in response to the erosion of global consensus, trade weaponisation and escalating conflicts across Europe and West Asia. Leaders of the European Union, Brazil, Kenya and Canada conceptualised the initiative, and India, Australia and Barbados co-sponsored it. It is designed as an open and flexible framework rather than another exclusive bloc or permanent bureaucracy. Its aims include strengthening international law, peace, multilateral cooperation and prosperity. It also seeks to enable countries from different political traditions to cooperate on reforming multilateral institutions and on common global challenges. At the same sidelines, India's External Affairs Minister took part in the 1st V4 plus India Foreign Ministers' Meeting, held during the Assembly week. India's position on reformed multilateralism was presented within this wider setting.

quizzes.title: Arctic Council: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Arctic has moved up the international agenda as melting ice opens new maritime corridors, including the Transpolar Sea Route. Control and influence over Arctic sea lanes are expected to shape future global trade and naval power projection. China describes itself as a near-Arctic state and is investing in Arctic research and infrastructure, while Russia has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline. The United States views Greenland as central to countering both. Greenland, the world's largest island, lies between North America and Europe, which gives it a strategic position for monitoring naval movements in the North Atlantic. Pituffik Space Base, formerly known as Thule Air Base, is a US facility for monitoring potential missile threats from Russia, China and North Korea. Denmark's firm stance highlights the tension between territorial sovereignty and the strategic ambitions of major powers. Within this wider competition, the Arctic Council is a platform through which countries discuss the region. Its members are the countries whose territory lies inside the Arctic area, and countries from outside the region also take part in its work. The Council gives these countries a place to talk through issues affecting the Arctic. Its discussions are reported in the booklet's coverage of Arctic affairs. Its members are not the only states with an interest in the region.

quizzes.title: India's Gender Gap Profile
quizzes.passage: The Global Gender Gap Index is an annual flagship publication of the World Economic Forum. It tracks the extent to which countries have closed gender disparities, rather than simply measuring women's absolute outcomes. The index has four dimensions: economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. Each nation is scored from 0 to 1, and the scores are expressed on a 0-100 scale, where 100 represents complete parity. In the 2026 report, India retained its position in the rankings. Its performance is uneven across the dimensions. In educational attainment and in health and survival, India's scores are close to complete parity, and the booklet describes near-complete parity between boys and girls in secondary and tertiary enrolment. Economic participation and political empowerment show far wider gaps. quizzes.title: Swachh Vayu Diwas Practice Quiz
quizzes.passage:
Swachh Vayu Diwas is an occasion that draws attention to clean air and to the measures taken against air pollution. It is observed alongside an international day that the United Nations General Assembly created to strengthen awareness and international action against air pollution. The occasion is also used to recognise progress, and awards are presented to cities and wards.

The National Clean Air Programme is a national-level strategy that addresses air pollution through coordinated interventions across sectors. It covers non-attainment cities as well as million-plus cities. A non-attainment city is one that has failed to comply with national ambient air quality standards over a specified assessment period.

Progress under the programme is reviewed through the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan, an annual assessment of cities. The assessment looks at road dust management, solid waste management, vehicular emissions, industrial emissions, construction and demolition waste, commercial sources, and public awareness and outreach. Cities are evaluated on key parameters that cover air quality, action plans and institutional capacity.

Cities are grouped by population into three categories. The first covers cities above 10 lakh people, the second covers cities between 3 and 10 lakh, and the third covers cities below 3 lakh. Rankings are announced separately for each category, so cities are compared with others of similar size.

quizzes.title: Pollution Control Tools and Laws Quiz
quizzes.passage:
India uses a mix of monitoring tools, field measures and legal provisions to tackle air pollution. The National Air Quality Index communicates air quality status in terms that are easy for people to understand, and it is a tool for effective communication with the public. SAFAR, the System of Air Quality and Weather Forecast and Research, monitors city-wide and localised air quality in Indian metropolises.

Field measures also address pollution from farms. Machines such as the Turbo Happy Seeder are used in the fields, and a bio-decomposer is used to turn crop residue into manure. Emergency action is taken under the Graded Response Action Plan, a set of measures designed to prevent further deterioration of air quality. Vehicle emission standards have been implemented nationwide to reduce vehicular emissions. Both the Turbo Happy Seeder and the Pusa Bio-Decomposer are field-level tools that deal with crop residue.

The legal base includes the Air Act, the Water Act and the Environment Protection Act, which are key pollution control regulations. The Constitution also links the environment to a fundamental duty of citizens, and it has been interpreted to protect the right to a healthy environment. Monitoring, field measures, emergency action and legal provisions together make up the framework described in the booklet.

quizzes.title: Orbits: LEO, MEO and GEO
quizzes.passage:
An orbit is the curved path that a satellite follows around Earth under the influence of gravity. Mission designers must weigh several trade-offs before they choose one, and no single orbit suits every purpose. Earth orbits are classified by altitude, by inclination and by shape. Shape refers to whether an orbit is circular or elliptical, and inclination refers to its tilt relative to the Equator.

Satellites are commonly grouped into three broad families. The first family is Low Earth Orbit, the closest of the three to the planet. Its satellites are widely used for Earth observation and communication, and crewed platforms such as the International Space Station also operate in this zone. Several sub-types exist for particular purposes, including the Sun-synchronous orbit and the Very Low Earth Orbit. Both of these are sub-types of Low Earth Orbit.

The second family is Medium Earth Orbit. Mission planners place it beyond the first family but below the third. The third family is Geosynchronous Orbit, and Geostationary Orbit is a special case within it. Geostationary Orbit is used for communication, weather and imaging. Each family is described in order of increasing distance from Earth, and each differs in altitude, latency and typical use.

quizzes.title: Reading Satellite Orbits
quizzes.passage:
An orbit is the curved path a satellite follows around Earth under the influence of gravity. Different orbits suit different missions, and the orbit a satellite uses determines the kind of work it can do. Earth orbits are classified by altitude, by inclination and by shape. Inclination is the tilt of an orbit relative to the Equator, and shape refers to whether an orbit is circular or elliptical. Some families lie close to the planet, while others lie far above it. Navigation systems also rely on satellites placed in one of these families.

The lowest family is often used for Earth observation and communication, and it suits large constellations of satellites. Low communication latency is a key feature of this family. Crewed space stations also operate in this closer region. Within the lowest family, specialised sub-types exist for particular purposes. Each family is linked to particular mission applications.

A middle family lies farther away than the lowest family. The highest family, known as geosynchronous, is defined by the timing of a satellite's revolution relative to the planet's spin. A special member of this family appears to hang above one place on the ground, which makes it useful for watching the same region continuously.

quizzes.title: EOS-05 Imaging Uses
quizzes.passage:
ISRO launched Earth Observation Satellite 05, known as EOS-05, from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota. The satellite is also called GISAT-1A, and the booklet describes it as India's first dedicated imaging satellite. It is designed to operate from a sub-geosynchronous orbit.

The launch validated India's cryogenic upper-stage technology for future human spaceflight, according to the booklet. The booklet also says it is the heaviest payload a GSLV has injected into orbit. Its launch was the nineteenth operational flight of the GSLV.

A low orbit satellite sees a given location only when it passes overhead, which leaves gaps between observations. A satellite that stays over one region of the planet can instead keep a wide area under watch for long periods. The booklet lists a fixed, 24/7 footprint over the Indian subcontinent as a geostationary advantage. Such platforms are described as useful for tracking cyclones, cloudbursts, flash floods and forest fires.

EOS-05 is equipped with optical and infrared imaging payloads, and its applications are presented under three headings: disaster management, strategic and national security, and agriculture and environment. Each heading is linked to a set of monitoring tasks, and the booklet lists examples under each one. The booklet presents these points together in a short summary of the satellite and its applications.

quizzes.title: EU Associate Membership Proposal
quizzes.passage: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed exploring a new form of relationship that could enable Canada to become an 'Associate Member' of the European Union. The proposal is linked to an 'Alliance for the Future', which would promote greater cooperation between Europe and Canada in areas such as defence, critical supply chains, technology, clean energy, strategic industries and Arctic security. The idea is presented as a possible new model of engagement between the EU and a non-EU country. Under such an arrangement, Canada could participate more closely in selected European frameworks without becoming a full member. Participation could cover selected EU programmes, cooperation in defence procurement and collaboration in emerging technologies. However, it would not automatically provide EU institutional membership, voting rights, representation in the European Parliament or automatic access to the Single Market. The term 'Associate Member' is not an established membership category under the EU's foundational treaties. One route would be formal treaty revision, which would require the relevant EU treaties to be amended. Such an arrangement could establish special economic cooperation, institutional dialogue and sector-specific integration without formally creating a new category of EU membership.

quizzes.title: Arms Control and Wildlife Trade Treaties
quizzes.passage:
The UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons is an arms-control framework that aims to restrict or prohibit weapons considered to have particularly harmful or indiscriminate effects. Countries meeting in Geneva recently reached a working definition of lethal autonomous weapons systems, commonly called killer robots. Such systems can identify and attack targets with limited or no meaningful human intervention. The Convention is commonly known as the Inhumane Weapons Convention, and India is a State Party to it.

The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, known as CITES, regulates international trade in endangered wild species. It is legally binding but does not override national laws, and its Conferences of the Parties review its decisions every two to three years. Its Secretariat functions under the UN Environment Programme. Parties appoint authorities for permits and scientific advice, and CITES species are listed by conservation status and trade sensitivity. India is among its members.

Ozone protection is governed by a separate set of agreements. The Vienna Convention was the first global treaty recognising ozone depletion. A landmark later agreement led to a near-complete phase-out of controlled ozone-depleting substances. The Kigali Amendment, adopted in 2016, followed as a further step in this framework.

Concerns over political funding transparency have intensified amid allegations involving registered unrecognised political parties. A political party can apply to the Election Commission of India for registration under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Registered parties must maintain records of specified contributions, file annual contribution reports and comply with audit and tax requirements. The Election Commission maintains and publishes information on registered, delisted and disputed parties, and such parties may receive certain electoral benefits.

The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 have been notified by the Department of Consumer Affairs. They make Indian Standard Time the single mandatory time reference for legal, administrative, commercial and official purposes across India. The rules are part of the 'One Nation, One Time' initiative, promote the use of NavIC and will come into force 180 days after their publication in the Official Gazette.

The estimates are prepared broadly in line with the UN System of National Accounts.
The revision uses 2019-20 as its new base year.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The first two statements match the booklet, while the base year is 2022-23, so only two are correct.

quizzes.title: National Accounts Series Facts
quizzes.passage: The economy heading in the September 2026 current affairs compilation has a single entry on national accounts. The entry describes India's revised National Accounts Series, which was released by a government statistics ministry. The revision introduces several methodological changes, which the entry lists in a short set of points. Among its aims, the revision seeks to incorporate structural changes in the economy. It also seeks to use improved and newer data sources and to update statistical methodologies. The entry describes a systematic framework for measuring an economy's activity. The item on the Upper Bhadra Project sits under the governance heading on the same booklet page. A further governance entry on that page concerns a proposed constitutional framework for a Union Territory. The compilation groups its items under headings such as governance, economy, environment and awards. The next booklet page opens with an environment item on India's first Blue Bond. The page is headed September 2026 and carries the label Topic in News. The national accounts entry is presented as a short list of points beneath its heading. The booklet's running header names the AILET Corner series. The item on the revised series is set in the economy section of the compilation.

questions.q: Which ministry released the revised National Accounts Series? (ministry name)
questions.answer: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
accept: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released the revised series.

questions.q: The revised series adopts which financial year as its new base year? (financial year)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 2022-23 as the new base year.

questions.q: Which deflation method is adopted for Manufacturing Gross Value Added in the revision? (method name)
questions.explanation: The revised series adopts double deflation for Manufacturing Gross Value Added.

questions.q: Which system are the revised estimates broadly prepared in line with? (name or abbreviation)
questions.answer: United Nations System of National Accounts
questions.explanation: The booklet says the estimates are prepared broadly in line with the United Nations System of National Accounts.

questions.q: National accounts give a framework for measuring an economy's production, income, expenditure, consumption, investment, saving and one further aspect. What is that aspect? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists external trade as the final item measured by national accounts.

questions.q: Which item on the same booklet page comes immediately before the national accounts entry? (name of item)
questions.explanation: The booklet places the Ladakh proposal in the governance section directly before the economy heading and its national accounts entry.

questions.q: What term describes the estimates that more accurately reflect the contemporary economy under the revision? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the revision aims for constant-price estimates that more accurately reflect the contemporary economy.
